The mirror image of Heap_Log2Floor: counts trailing zeros, narrowing by 16, 8 and 4 bits when the low half is zero, then adds g_ctzNibble[x & 0xf] from 0x57e6e0 = {0,0,1,0,2,0,1,0,3,0,1,0,2,0,1,0}. Returns 28 for x = 0. No callers and no references (dead code).

name: Heap_BitmapFill
comment: void __thiscall Heap_BitmapFill(Heap *this, u32 *bitmap, u32 nBits) -- Sets nBits>>5 whole words to 0xffffffff. If nBits & 31 is non-zero, the next word gets only its TOP (nBits&31) bits set: ~((1 << (32 - r)) - 1). This is MSB-first, matching Heap_AllocSmall/Heap_FreeSmall (set bit = free slot). ECX (this) is loaded by the caller but unused. ret 8. The only caller is Heap_InitSmallPools 0x54d9c2.

name: Heap_CarveBlock
comment: void __thiscall Heap_CarveBlock(Heap *this, HeapBlock *block, u32 blockSize, u32 need) -- Takes `need` bytes (header included) from the free block `block` of size blockSize. rem = blockSize - need. - rem >= 0x18: split. The tail at block+need becomes a free block that takes over block's place in the list. block->next->prev = tail; tail->next = block->next; tail->prev = tail if block is the head (and the head becomes tail), otherwise block->prev, with block->prev->next = tail. Tail header = rem|2, footer = rem at its end, and bit 0 is set on the block after it. Then block->hdr -= rem + 2, which leaves size = need and clears the free bit. - rem < 0x18: the whole block is handed out. freeCount--. Unlink: if it is the head, head = next and head->prev = head; otherwise prev->next = next and next->prev = prev. The next physical header is decremented by 1, a subtraction rather than a bit-clear, which relies on the invariant that its bit 0 is set. block->hdr -= 2. ret 0xc. Callers: Heap_Alloc and Heap_AllocAligned.

name: Heap_FindPrevBlock
comment: HeapBlock * __thiscall Heap_FindPrevBlock(Heap *this, HeapBlock *block) -- Walks the blocks in address order from this->firstBlock (+0x0), stepping by (hdr & 0x0ffffffc), and returns the last block whose successor is >= `block`, i.e. the block just before it. This is O(number of blocks). If `block` is the first block, it returns the first block itself. ret 4. The only caller is Heap_AllocAligned, to hand a small alignment gap to the preceding block.

name: Heap_AllocAligned
comment: void * __thiscall Heap_AllocAligned(Heap *this, u32 size, u32 align) -- Aligned allocation. align must be a power of 2. If align <= alignMask+1 it simply returns Heap_Alloc(size). Otherwise: size = max(size, 8); payload = (size + alignMask) & ~alignMask. It walks freeCount nodes from the head with the same halving counter as Heap_Alloc. For each block it computes off = ((blk + 8 + align-1) & ~(align-1)) - blk, and keeps the candidate with the smallest off among blocks of size <= the best so far and >= payload + off. gap = off - 8, need = payload + 8, nb = blk + gap. - gap == 0: CarveBlock(blk). - gap >= 0x18: blk shrinks to a free block of size gap, keeping its place in the list. nb becomes a new free block (size best-gap) linked right after it; freeCount++. CarveBlock(nb), then nb->hdr |= 1. - 0 < gap < 0x18: blk is unlinked. Heap_FindPrevBlock(blk)->hdr += gap (the preceding allocated block absorbs the gap). nb is pushed as the new head (size best-gap), then CarveBlock(nb). The header then gets |= (Heap_Log2Floor(align) - 2) << 28, the +4 word = 0x98765432, and it returns nb+8. Returns NULL if nothing fits. ret 8. No callers and no data references (dead code).

name: Heap_Free
comment: void __thiscall Heap_Free(Heap *this, void *ptr) -- Frees a block, merging it with free neighbours. - If smallBase(+0x30) <= ptr < smallEnd(+0x38), it goes to Heap_FreeSmall 0x54e767 instead. - Otherwise b = ptr-8; prev = b - (b->hdr & 1 ? *(u32*)(b-4) : 0); next = b + (b->hdr & 0x0ffffffc). - prev free: prev grows to cover b, and next too if next is free. next is unlinked (if it is the head: head = next->next, head->prev = head) and freeCount--. prev keeps its list position and gets the free header, footer and bit 0 on the block after it. - only next free: b takes over next's list position (if next was the head, b->prev = b and head = b), with size b + next; freeCount is unchanged. - neither free: b is pushed on the head (b->next = old head, b->prev = b, oldHead->prev = b); freeCount++. No NULL check, no check of the 0x98765432 magic, no double-free detection. ret 4. Callers: Scenaric_Free 0x50d629 (ECX=0x6cff98), List_FreeNode 0x5473d0 and 0x547415 (ECX=0x6defa8), and Heap_TermSmallPools.

name: Heap_AllocSmall
comment: void * __thiscall Heap_AllocSmall(Heap *this, u32 size) -- Bitmap-pool allocation. - cls = ceil(log2 size) via Heap_Log2Floor, adding 1 unless size is exactly a power of 2. - pool = cls > smallMinShift(+0x2c) ? cls - smallMinShift : 0. - addr = smallBase(+0x30) + (pool << smallPoolShift(+0x2e)); w = smallBitmaps(+0x3c)[pool]. - Scans ((+0x28 >> pool) + 31) >> 5 words; addr advances by +0x1c << (pool+5) for each zero word. - On the first non-zero word: bit = Heap_Log2Floor(*w); *w ^= 1 << bit; returns addr + ((31 - bit) << (smallMinShift + pool)). - Returns 0 if the pool is full. It does not try a larger pool; Heap_Alloc then falls back to the free list. The pool index is not bounded here; Heap_Alloc guarantees it only because size <= +0x20. There is no enabled check, so it dereferences +0x3c even when it is NULL. ret 4. The only caller is Heap_Alloc.

name: Heap_FreeSmall
comment: void __thiscall Heap_FreeSmall(Heap *this, void *ptr) -- Small-block free for the bitmap pools. Heap_Free 0x54e2f1 calls it when smallBase(+0x30) <= ptr < smallEnd(+0x38). off = ptr - smallBase; pool = off >> u16 poolShift(+0x2e); slot = (off - (pool << poolShift)) >> (u16 minShift(+0x2c) + pool); then smallBitmaps(+0x3c)[pool][slot >> 5] |= 0x80000000 >> (slot & 31). A SET bit means the slot is free: the allocator 0x54e63d finds a set bit and XORs it off. Pool i therefore holds slots of 1 << (minShift + i) bytes. No double-free check and no alignment check (a pointer inside a slot frees that slot). ret 4.

name: Menu_IsDirty
comment: int Menu_IsDirty(void) -- Returns bit 0 of g_menuFlags 0x6e38c4 as a signed 1-bit bitfield (shl 31; sar 31 -> 0 or -1). No callers and no data references, so the menu dirty bit is write-only in the retail build.

name: Menu_SetDirty
comment: void Menu_SetDirty(u32 on) -- g_menuFlags = (g_menuFlags & ~1) | (on & 1). Menu_Update calls it with 0 after drawing; the option handlers 0x542fc5 and 0x543aa8 call it with 1.

name: Menu_GetItemIndex
comment: s16 Menu_GetItemIndex(MenuPage *item) -- NULL -> 0xFFFF (-1, meaning 'no parent / root'); otherwise (item - g_menuPages) >> 3, the node index in the current menu's 8-byte node array. Used by Menu_AddItems and Menu_AddPage to store the parent index.

name: Menu_FindPrevSibling
comment: s16 Menu_FindPrevSibling(s16 idx) -- Scans backwards from idx-1 for a node with the same parent (+2) that is not disabled (flags bit 3). Disabled matches are skipped. If the scan reaches index 0 without a match it returns idx unchanged (the caller then wraps with Menu_FindLastChild). Only caller: Menu_Update on UP (pad mask 0xFFEF, auto-repeat). It would read items[-1] only if node 0 (the root) were disabled, which Menu_AddPage never sets.

name: Menu_FindNextSibling
comment: s16 Menu_FindNextSibling(s16 idx) -- If idx+1 == g_menuItemCount it returns idx. Otherwise it scans forward while (parent differs AND i < count-1) OR node i is disabled (bit 3), and returns i if items[i].parent == items[idx].parent, else idx (the caller wraps with Menu_FindFirstChild). If the last node is disabled the scan steps to items[count], one node past the used part of the array. Caller: Menu_Update on DOWN (0xFFBF).

name: Menu_FindFirstChild
comment: s16 Menu_FindFirstChild(s16 page) -- From index 1 forward, returns the first non-disabled node whose parent == page; if none is found it falls back to 1 (whatever node 1 is). Used when entering a page, for DOWN wrap-around, by Menu_ResetToRoot, and by Menu_Update's move off a disabled cursor.

name: Menu_FindLastChild
comment: s16 Menu_FindLastChild(s16 page) -- From g_menuItemCount-1 backwards, returns the last non-disabled node whose parent == page. If nothing matches it stops at index 0 and returns it (the root). UP wrap-around in Menu_Update.

name: Menu_AddItems
comment: s16 __cdecl Menu_AddItems(MenuPage *page, MenuHandler handler, ...) -- Varargs list of handlers ending in 0. For each handler it appends node g_menuPages[g_menuItemCount] with flags = (flags & 0xFC) | 1 (kind 1 = leaf/value item) | 4 (has handler) & ~8 & ~0x10, parent = Menu_GetItemIndex(page), +4 = handler. It then does page->childCount++, g_menuItemCount++ and g_curMenu->count(+4)++, and sets g_menuFlags bit 0. Returns the index of the first new node. Byte +1 is not cleared, the page pointer is not NULL-checked, and there is no check against the Menu capacity (+6). Callers: Menu_BuildConfirmMenu, 0x539199, the pause-menu builder 0x5436eb, the 'PAUSED' builder 0x5465c1.

name: Menu_AddPage
comment: MenuPage *Menu_AddPage(MenuPage *parent, void *labelOrHandler, u8 hasHandler) -- Appends a kind-0 node (a page/submenu that CROSS enters): flags &= 0xFC, bit 2 = hasHandler, bits 3 and 4 cleared, +4 = labelOrHandler (a char* title such as 'PAUSE' 0x57c178 or '--' 0x57c048 when hasHandler is 0, else a MenuHandler that draws it), parent = Menu_GetItemIndex(parent) (-1 for NULL = root), childCount = 0. If a parent is given it does parent->childCount++; always g_menuItemCount++ and g_curMenu->count++. Returns the new node. No capacity check.

name: Menu_SetItemColor
comment: void Menu_SetItemColor(s16 idx) -- Text_SetColor(0x3030C0) when idx == g_menuCursor, else Text_SetColor(0x808080). Only used by Menu_Update's layout 0, the debug-font page layout that no retail caller uses.

name: Menu_Init
comment: void Menu_Init(Menu *menu) -- Resets the menu globals: count, capacity, lastCursor, curPage and prevPage to 0, g_menuCursor = 1, the capture bytes and cursor row to 0, g_curMenu = menu. It does NOT load g_menuPages from the record: the zeroed state reaches the record the next time Menu_SetCurrent saves it. It then sends message 8 (INIT) to every node of menu->items (count = record +4) that has flag bit 2 set. Called by Load_DAVnWAR 0x548097 and Load_FreeLevel 0x5481d0, both with g_pauseMenu 0x57c128.

name: Menu_ResetToRoot
comment: void Menu_ResetToRoot(Menu *menu, s16 cursor) -- menu->curPage(+0xC) = 0, g_menuCurPage = 0, marks dirty. If cursor == -1 it sets menu->cursor(+8) = Menu_FindFirstChild(0) and g_menuCursor = that; otherwise g_menuCursor = cursor. g_menuCursorRow = 0. It assumes menu is already current. Callers: PauseMenu_Open 0x542afa and 0x546515 (both -1), 0x542ac0 (explicit index).

name: Menu_SetCurrent
comment: void Menu_SetCurrent(Menu *menu) -- Marks dirty. If g_curMenu != NULL it saves g_menuCursor, g_menuLastCursor, g_menuCurPage and g_menuPrevPage into g_curMenu +8/+0xA/+0xC/+0xE; count is not saved because the add functions update the record directly. It then sets g_curMenu = menu and loads g_menuPages = menu->items, count(+4), capacity(+6), cursor(+8), lastCursor(+0xA), curPage(+0xC) and prevPage(+0xE). Capture state and cursor row are left untouched. 8 callers: the menu builders, PauseMenu_Open, 0x546515, Ui_DrawTextBox and Ui_DrawMenuBox (these two with g_confirmPage 0x6de160 before Menu_Update).

name: Menu_PrintPath
comment: void Menu_PrintPath(MenuPage *page) -- Recursive breadcrumb: if page->parent != -1 it recurses on g_menuPages[parent] first, then does Text_SetColor(0x803030) and Text_PrintFmt("%s" 0x57e6f0, page->handlerOrLabel). It prints the +4 word as a string even for nodes that hold a handler. Only reached from Menu_Update layout 0, which retail never uses.

name: Menu_SetCapture
comment: void Menu_SetCapture(u8 captureMode, int notifyOnRelease) -- Does not poll input. It copies g_padMenuPrev = g_padMenuCur, so no Pad_MenuPressed edge fires this frame, calls InputMgr_ResetEdges(&0x6d6780), then g_menuCapturePrev = g_menuCapture and g_menuCapture = captureMode (0 none, 1 item owns input while the menu is still drawn, 2 item owns input and the menu is hidden). On a release (new mode 0, old mode != 0) with notifyOnRelease set and cursor flag bit 2 set it sends message 10 to the cursor node. Menu_Update will send message 10 again on its next call because g_menuCapturePrev is still non-zero, so handlers get two release messages. The callers pass (2,0), (1,0), (0,1) and (0,0): the option handlers, Menu_RebindControl, 0x542ac0.

name: Menu_NotifyPageChange
comment: void Menu_NotifyPageChange(void) -- Marks dirty, then sends message 5 (UNFOCUS) to node g_menuPrevPage and message 4 (FOCUS) to node g_menuCurPage, each only if that node has flag bit 2. Called after entering a page (Menu_Update) and by Menu_GoBack.

name: Menu_GoBack
comment: void Menu_GoBack(void) -- If the current page's parent is < 0 (already at the root) it clears g_gameFlags bits 0x21 (GF_PAUSE_TOGGLE plus bit 0). Otherwise: prevPage = curPage; cursor = curPage (the submenu entry you came from stays highlighted); curPage = that node's parent. Always ends with Menu_NotifyPageChange. Callers: Menu_Update on TRIANGLE, 0x543683, 0x54402f, 0x5452e3.

name: Menu_Update
comment: u32 Menu_Update(int layout, u8 align) -- Per-frame menu draw and input. Font: 2 if paused (g_gameFlags & 0x40), else 0 (Debug) for layout 0 and 1 (Game) otherwise. If capture==0 && capturePrev!=0 it sends message 10 to the cursor node without checking bit 2, clears capturePrev and marks dirty. Otherwise it sends message 9 each frame while capture!=0. Unless capture==2 it draws. Layout 0 prints the breadcrumb (Menu_PrintPath) and a newline; layouts 1 and 2 set colour 0x4BCCFF. rows = (g_textWinH - g_textCursorY)/lineHeight - 1, scrolled so that g_menuCursorRow stays visible. It moves the 0x10 'selected' bit from lastCursor to cursor. Layout 1 centres the list vertically when childCount < rows. For each child of curPage (loop driven by the page's childCount): message 7 (pre-draw) if it has a handler, colour 0xA0A0A0 if disabled, then either Text_PrintfStyled(align, blink = (cursor && layout != 0), "%s", label) or message 0 (draw), plus message 6 for the cursor node. Afterwards Menu_SetDirty(0). On a focus change it sends 5 to the old node and 4 to the new one. Input only when capture==0: UP/DOWN (Pad_MenuRepeat 0xFFEF/0xFFBF) move with wrap and play Ui_PlayMoveSound. Kind 0 + CROSS (Pad_MenuPressed 0xBFFF) plays Ui_PlayConfirmSound (even on a disabled node); if the node is enabled it sends message 3 if it has a handler and enters the page (cursor = first child, Menu_NotifyPageChange), returning 1. Kind 1: LEFT 0xFF7F -> 1, RIGHT 0xFFDF -> 2, otherwise CROSS -> confirm sound + 3 unless g_letterboxState == 1; then LEFT/RIGHT also -> 11 (value changed). TRIANGLE 0xEFFF: cancel sound, message 12, Menu_GoBack, returns 1. Finally a disabled cursor is moved to the first child of curPage and the colour is reset to 0x4BCCFF. Callers: Ui_DrawTextBox and Ui_DrawMenuBox (2,2) and the pause draw 0x54579d (1,2) from Game_Frame_2, so layout 0 is never used.

name: Menu_Close
comment: void Menu_Close(void) -- Called by PauseMenu_Exit. If capture != 0 it sends message 10 to the cursor node (no bit-2 check), clears its 0x10 bit, sets g_menuCursor = 0 and capture = 0. Then, if the cursor node has flag bit 2, it sends message 12 (CANCEL).

name: TextResBank_Ctor
comment: TextResBank *__thiscall TextResBank_Ctor(TextResBank *this) -- vtbl = 0x5771bc, loaded(+4) = 0, count(+6) = 0, entries(+8) = NULL; returns this. Its only caller is StaticInit_g_6d656c_ctor 0x52293e, for the global g_textCatalog 0x6d656c.

name: TextResBank_Dtor
comment: void __thiscall TextResBank_Dtor(TextResBank *this) -- Resets vtbl to 0x5771bc, frees entries[i].text (+8 of each 0xC entry) for i < count with CRT delete 0x565d43, then frees the entries array. Callers: StaticDtor_g_6d656c 0x52295f, TextResBank_DeletingDtor.

name: TextResBank_Load
comment: u16 __thiscall TextResBank_Load(TextResBank *this, const char *path) -- Bs_LoadFile(path, &size). On failure: MessageBoxA("Could not load file: " + path, "BSM File Error", MB_ICONHAND), loaded = 0, count = 0. On success with size > 0: copies 12 bytes and strncmp's them with "GREETINGV1.0" 0x57e720. If they match it reads u32 n, allocates n*0xC entries, and for each entry reads u32 key and u32 len, then text = operator new(len) and strncpy(len) (NULL text when len == 0). Finally loaded = 1, count = (u16)n. If the magic does not match: MessageBoxA("Could not load file, check version"). The magic copy and the file buffer are freed. Returns count. No bounds check against the file size, the count is truncated to u16, and there is no free of an earlier table. WinMain 0x4013b2 calls it once with g_levelBasePath-style prefix + "GREET_txt.BSM".

name: TextResBank_LoadString
comment: char *__thiscall TextResBank_LoadString(TextResBank *this, u16 group, u16 langMask, u16 index) -- The key compared is group<<24 + index<<8 + langMask. Every caller passes a language mask (g_langMask 0x57910a or the menu copy 0x6dedf0) as the 2nd argument, and the disc file confirms the low byte is the single-bit language (0x01000101 EN title, 0x01000102 FR 'Une Faim de Loup'). It linear-searches when loaded == 1 and returns a newly allocated operator-new copy of the text (len bytes), or NULL. The caller owns the copy, and none of the 23 callers frees it.

name: TextResBank_DeletingDtor
comment: TextResBank *__thiscall TextResBank_DeletingDtor(TextResBank *this, u32 flags) -- Scalar deleting destructor, the only vtable slot of 0x5771bc: TextResBank_Dtor, then operator delete(this) if flags & 1; returns this; ret 4.

name: StaticInit_g_animPartMatrices
comment: void StaticInit_g_animPartMatrices(void) -- CRT dynamic initializer, listed in the .data initializer table at 0x5790b8 between 0x54a6b4 and 0x55b1a0. It calls StaticInit_g_animPartMatrices_ctor.

name: StaticInit_g_animPartMatrices_ctor
comment: void StaticInit_g_animPartMatrices_ctor(void) -- Constructs g_animPartMatrices: loops 42 (0x2A) times with stride 0x40 from 0x6e38d0, calling the trivial matrix constructor Thunk_ReturnArg 0x4077f0 (ecx = element), which initialises nothing. The array is the per-draw part-matrix scratch buffer of Instance_DrawAnimParts.

name: Anim_StartDirect
comment: u32 Anim_StartDirect(ScnInstance *inst, Animator *anim, u16 directIndex, int mode) -- Starts an animation from the model's DIRECT list: data = *(u32*)(model(inst+4)+0x10 table + 4 + directIndex*4), with no count check. NULL returns 0 without touching the animator. Otherwise anim->data = it, animId(+0x1A) = directIndex, acc(+0x10) = 0. Mode 0: frame(+0x1C) = 1 % keyCount, Anim_DecodeFirstKey into bufA(+4) and bufC(+0xC), duration(+0x1E) = Anim_DecodeKey(bufA, frame). Mode 1 (blend): frame = 0, swap bufA/bufC, duration = Anim_DecodeFirstKey(bufB). Other modes only set data/id/acc. Flags are not touched. Returns 1. Only caller: the animator init 0x55b3ae, with (inst, anim, 0, 0), as the fallback when no mapped id starts.

name: Anim_GetCurrentKey
comment: AnimKey *Anim_GetCurrentKey(Animator *anim) -- Walks the key records from anim->data + 0xA, stepping 8 + 2*payloadWords(+4) bytes, frame(+0x1C) times, and returns the current key record. No callers (dead).

name: Anim_GetNextKey
comment: AnimKey *Anim_GetNextKey(Animator *anim, u16 frame) -- Same walk to index (frame + 1) % keyCount(data+8); returns that record. No callers (dead).

name: Anim_GetDebugNames
comment: void Anim_GetDebugNames(ScnInstance *inst, u16 animId, const char **modelName, const char **animName) -- Looks up printable names in the WAR type-0x86 table g_animNameTable 0x585050: {s16 modelCount; per model {s16 modelKey; s16 animCount; char name[] (NUL, padded to 2 bytes); per anim {s16 animId; char name[] (padded)}}}. It matches modelKey against inst->record[0] (the model resource index, via inst+0x1C) and the anim id against animId. Defaults are "<unknown>" 0x57e764 for both outputs (also when the table pointer is NULL). Only used to feed Debug_Printf("Cannot find AnimID %d, Model %s, Anim %s\n") in Anim_Start and Anim_GetDurationMs; Debug_Printf is a no-op in retail.

name: Anim_RestorePose
comment: void Anim_RestorePose(Animator *anim) -- Rebuilds the three pose buffers from a restored frame index. prev = frame - 1 (0 if frame == 0). It decodes key 0 into bufA and swaps A/B, then replays Anim_DecodeKey(bufB, i) for i = 1..prev into bufB. It then decodes key 0 into bufA and swaps again, so bufA = pose at prev and bufB = key 0, and replays 1..frame into bufB. Finally Anim_InterpolatePose writes bufC. Durations returned by the decoders are ignored (the caller restored +0x1E), but the decoders do overwrite pendingEvent(+0x14). Only caller: 0x562340, which Cine_Finish 0x5620a0 uses to put an actor's saved animation state back after a cinematic.

name: Anim_Advance
comment: The only reader of g_animDt (= g_dt*250, exact). Accumulates acc(+0x10) += g_animDt * speed(u16 +0x20, 4.12) >> 12 and, in a while loop, subtracts frameDuration(u16 +0x1e)<<10 per key-frame advance, carrying the remainder; sets flag 8 in +0x22 on wrap (animation ended), which is what most state machines test ('*(ushort*)(obj+0x62) & 8'). Because the remainder is carried, animation length in game time is frame-rate independent (only the >>12 of the speed product truncates, <1/1024 ms per frame). So anim-end-gated transitions keep true time while g_dtMs-gated ones stretch at high FPS.

name: Anim_PostInitStub
comment: void Anim_PostInitStub(ScnInstance *inst, Animator *anim) -- Empty: push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; ret (no FPU result). Called once by the animator init at 0x55b4b0 after the first animation is chosen. Probably a hook left over from the PS1 version (inferred).

name: Anim_GetRootOffset
comment: void Anim_GetRootOffset(ScnInstance *inst, Animator *anim, Vec3s *out) -- v = model(inst+4)->joints(+0x14)[0].offset (s16 at +2/+4/+6) + displayed pose(anim+0xC)[0].pos (+0xC/+0x10/+0x14). It rotates v by Mat44_SetRotXZY(inst rot +0x10/+0x12/+0x14, each & 0xFFF, via Math_Angle4096ToRadians), divides each component by 8.0 (0x574398) and stores __ftol-truncated s16 into out. Instance position is not added, so the result is the animated root-joint offset in world units relative to the object. Callers: Wolf_Fx5_Start 0x491566 and ScnMobile_UpdateShadow 0x51186d, so blob shadows follow the root joint.

name: Instance_CalcWorldMatrix
comment: void Instance_CalcWorldMatrix(ScnInstance *inst, Camera *cam, Vec3s *scale6_10OrNull, D3DMATRIX *out) -- Attached instance (inst flags & 8): link = inst+0x20. If link flags(+7) & 1 is clear it clears inst flag 1 (not drawn) and leaves out unwritten. Otherwise out = link matrix(+0x20); flag 0x08 replaces the translation with out applied to link local offset(+0/+2/+4)*8; flag 0x20 adds link world offset(+0x10/+0x12/+0x14)*8; then it sets inst flag 1. Normal instance: out = (S * R) * T. S = Mat44_SetScale(Math_Fixed10ToFloat_s16 of scale) or identity. R = Mat44_SetRotXZY(rot & 0xFFF). T = translation(pos(+8/+0xA/+0xC) * 8.0). In mirror mode (g_mirrorRenderFlag 0x6d6fe4 == -1 || g_mirrorRenderOn 0x6d6fe8 == 1) R's Y column (m01, m11, m21) is negated and pos.z(+0xA) is temporarily replaced by g_mirrorPlaneY2x 0x6d6fea - y. Visibility: p = cam->viewMat(+0x40) * pos (unscaled world units, __ftol to s16) + boundCenter(+0x24/+0x26/+0x28), passed with extent(+0x2A) to 0x55cae3(inst, &p, extent, 1), which sets or clears inst flag 1. Mirror y is restored afterwards.

name: Instance_DrawAnimParts
comment: void Instance_DrawAnimParts(ScnInstance *inst, Animator *anim, Camera *cam, Vec3s *scaleOrNull) -- Builds O with Instance_CalcWorldMatrix, then IDirect3DDevice7::SetTransform(VIEW = 2, &cam->viewMat) through g_pD3DAppMain+0x28, vtable +0x2C. It returns if inst flag 1 (visible) is cle

name: Anim_InterpolatePose
comment: void Anim_InterpolatePose(Animator *anim) -- t = (float)acc(+0x10) / (float)(duration(+0x1E) << 10), with no clamp and no zero check. For each joint < jointCount(+0x18): C(bufC) = lerp(A(bufA), B(bufB), t). For the 3 angles: d = B - A, then if d > PI d -= 2PI, if d < -PI d += 2PI; c = A + d*t, then +2PI once if negative, else subtract 2PI while >= 2PI (constants -PI/2PI/PI at 0x5743c8/cc/d0). Position and scale use plain lerp. Channels(+0x24) are copied from B; +0x26 is not written. Called first thing by Anim_Advance (before time is added) and by Anim_RestorePose.

name: Anim_DecodeFirstKey
comment: u16 Anim_DecodeFirstKey(Animator *anim, AnimJointPose *dest) -- Decodes key record 0 (anim->data + 0xA) into dest and returns its duration (u16 +0). pendingEvent(+0x14) = key0.eventId (+6), even when that is 0. For each of entryCount(+2) entries starting at +8: joint = ctrl & 0x3F (not checked against jointCount); the joint is reset to rot 0, pos 0, scale 1.0 with channels = ctrl; then the present channels are read in bit order. 16-bit mode: rot 0x54a230 (-(2*PI*s16)/4096, +2PI if negative), pos (float)s16, scale Math_U16ToUnitFloat (u16/1024). 8-bit mode (ctrl & 0x8000): rot 0x54a276 (s8, /128), pos (float)s8, scale 0x54a2d4 (u8/128), and the pointer is re-aligned to 2 bytes after the entry. Joints not listed keep whatever dest held.

name: Anim_DecodeKey
comment: u16 Anim_DecodeKey(Animator *anim, const AnimJointPose *src, u16 keyIndex) -- dest = anim->bufB(+8). It does memcpy(dest, src, jointCount*0x28) (0x565e70), walks to key keyIndex (8 + 2*payloadWords per step, no bounds check), sets pendingEvent only if that key's eventId != 0, and decodes its entries exactly as Anim_DecodeFirstKey does. The effect is sparse joint replacement on top of the previous key pose. Returns the key duration. Callers: Anim_Start, Anim_StartDirect, Anim_Advance, Anim_RestorePose.

name: Anim_ClearPose
comment: void Anim_ClearPose(Animator *anim, AnimJointPose *pose) -- Dead helper (no callers). Loops jointCount(+0x18) times writing rot = 0, pos = 0, scale = 1024.0f (0x44800000, not 1.0) and channels = 0, but never advances the pointer, so it only ever rewrites element 0. Looks like a stale leftover from fixed-point 1024 = 1.0 scale (inferred).

name: Camera_OnManualRotate
comment: void Camera_OnManualRotate(s32 dir) -- Called with the yaw input value whenever the player turns the camera: from UpdateFollow, UpdateSamChase, UpdateLook and UpdateDirected; every call site pushes it. It zeroes turn state 0x6e43d6, blocked counters 0x6e43f1/0x6e4420 and collision-frame counter 0x6e43de. It sets 0x6e43f4 bit3 = (dir<0) and bit4 = (dir>0). If bit3 it invalidates the positive-side block position 0x6e4412..16 (0x8000). If bit4 it invalidates the negative-side block position 0x6e440c..10. It sets 0x6e43fc = 10000 and zeroes the auto-turn rates 0x6e43c8/cc/d0.

name: Camera_ShakeOffset
comment: 3 Rand(2s) per call while amplitude s != 0; shake started by Camera_StartShake 0x55262a, stopped by 0x55264c. A second inlined copy lives in the CannonBall camera function 0x4a3b4f, so during cannonball flight the shake clock can be advanced twice per frame and 6 values drawn per frame. RNG position after any shake is frame-rate dependent (3 x frames).

name: Camera_StopShake
comment: void Camera_StopShake(void) -- Zeroes shake amplitude 0x6e4380, duration 0x6e4378 and elapsed 0x6e437c. Callers: CannonBall_Update and Camera_Reset 0x559ff1.

name: Camera_StickAxisDeadzone
comment: s16 Camera_StickAxisDeadzone(u8 raw) -- v = raw - 0x80. If |v| <= 40 (0x28) it returns 0. Otherwise it returns v-40 or v+40, giving a range of about -88..+87. Its only caller is the debug branch of Camera_Update (g_camDebugMode not 0 and not 2): leftX moves eye x, leftY moves eye z, rightY moves pitch and rightX moves yaw, on analog pads (type nibble 7).

name: Camera_OrbitInstance_Unused
comment: void Camera_OrbitInstance_Unused(Camera *cam, const u16 *inst) -- DEAD CODE: no callers and no pointer reference in the exe. It sets eye = Mat34s_FromEulerYXZ(0x1000-pitch, yaw+0x800, 0) transposed times (0,0,cam->dist), the same as Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles about the origin. If inst[0] & 4 it adds inst[4..6] and inst[0x12..0x14]; if inst is an Instance embedded at ScnObject+4 those are ScnObject.pos (+0xC) and boundCenter (+0x28), which is inferred. It then sets roll 0 and calls Camera_BuildViewMatrix(cam, g_pZeroVec3s).

name: Camera_UpdateDebugFreeCam
comment: void Camera_UpdateDebugFreeCam(Camera *cam, Pad *pad, Pad *pad2) -- Developer free camera, run when g_camDebugMode == 2. That byte has no writer. Behaviour: - If pad2 is type 1 (PS1 mouse): buttons 0xF4FF move the camera forward, 0xF8FF move it back, and signed bytes pad2+0x2e/+0x2f subtract from yaw and add to pitch. - When !Map_IsOpen() && !(g_gameFlags & 1), pad buttons act: L1 (0x400) and L2 (0x100) move along the full 3D view direction (rot row 2). Left/right strafe along the XZ right vector (row 0). Up/down move along the XZ forward vector; if the camera looks straight down it uses -row 1. R1 and R2 move vertically. Speed is g_dt*1000 >> 12, i.e. 1000 units/s. - The analog left stick (Pad_AnalogToStick) also moves, without the gate. - Square/Circle and the right stick (Pad_StickToDeadzonedAxes) turn yaw; Triangle/Cross turn pitch. The rate is g_camModeParams[0].yawSpeed (1500/s). - Roll is set to 0, then Camera_BuildViewMatrix(cam, zero).

name: Camera_SweepEyeBox
comment: u16 Camera_SweepEyeBox(const Vec3s *eye, const s16 *boxMinMax, Vec3s *ioDelta, const Vec3s *target, Vec3s *outTried) -- Moves the camera box (min at boxMinMax[0..2] = 0x6e45e8, max at [4..6] = 0x6e45f0) from eye by *ioDelta, with sliding. It runs at most 4 iterations. - Each iteration halves the remaining delta until every axis is below 26 (0x1a) and adds that sub-step to *outTried. - It calls Collide_SweepBox(0, box, step, &frac, &outY, contacts, 0, flags 2, ...). - On no hit the whole sub-step is taken. On a hit it moves by frac and classifies each contact into 0x6d549a[i]: normal.y >= -0xb54 gives 2 (wall); otherwise a floor contact gives 4 when the support-point dot is < -0x800 and 1 when it is not. - If there is a floor-type contact within 20 units of the box bottom, it steps up onto the floor (vertical = floorY - bottom - 1). - Otherwise it slides: it projects out the normals of type-1 contacts; with walls only it projects type-2 contacts toward the target plane. - For each wall it records which side of the view it is on (centroid minus g_camPos, dotted with g_camera.viewMatS row 0): bit 2 for <1, bit 1 otherwise. - On return, *ioDelta = actual displacement. The returned u16 is the OR of contact classes (1 floor, 2 wall, 4 edge), plus 0x400 or 0x800 when all walls lie on one side. - Uses the shared collision scratch 0x6d5468..0x6d54a9 with its own layout. The Ghidra names g_contactClass, g_wolfTmpRot and g_wolfTmpStep printed there are wrong for this function. - Only caller: Camera_SolveCollision.

name: Camera_ProbeLedgeAhead
comment: bool Camera_ProbeLedgeAhead(const Vec3s *angles) -- Returns 0 unless request flag 0x6e45be bit0 is set. It casts Collide_RayCastStatic with maxDist 0x114 (276). The origin is (reqTarget.x, reqTarget.y-60, reqTarget.z). The direction is row 2 of Mat34s_FromEulerYXZ(pitch = 0x2aa (60 deg, fixed), yaw = angles[1], roll = angles[2]). angles[0] is ignored. It returns 1 when the hit distance is > 0x113, i.e. nothing within 276 units. INFERRED meaning: Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles places the eye with (-pitch, yaw+0x800), so this ray points forward and 60 deg DOWN from Ralph's head. A clear ray means no floor ahead-below (a ledge or drop).

name: Camera_UpdateLedgeLook
comment: void Camera_UpdateLedgeLook(Camera *cam) -- 4-state debounce on g_camLedgeLookState 0x6e4382, using Camera_ProbeLedgeAhead with yaw = cam yaw if settings 0x6e45e4 & 0x10, else request yaw 0x6e45ba. - State 0: clear gives 1. - State 1: blocked gives 2. - State 2: blocked gives 3, clear gives 1. - State 3: blocked gives 0, clear gives 2. In state 3 it also computes pitch = cam pitch - 0xaa clamped to >= g_camMinPitch, but Camera_ProbeLedgeAhead ignores the pitch, so that computation is dead. Camera_UpdateFollow calls it only when settings bit 0x8 is set and no trajectory is active (else state = 0). It then uses the state for the desired pitch: 0 = g_camMinPitch (0xA0), 1 = 0x2aa (60 deg), 2 or 3 = hold current.

name: Camera_ClampAngleToArc
comment: bool Camera_ClampAngleToArc(s16 *angle, s16 lo, s16 hi) -- Arc test with wrap: if hi < lo the angle is out of range when hi < a < lo; otherwise it is out of range when a < lo or a > hi. When out of range it snaps *angle to whichever of lo or hi is nearer in wrapped angular distance and returns 1. Otherwise it returns 0.

name: Camera_ApplyRestriction
comment: void Camera_ApplyRestriction(Vec3s *angles, s32 speeds[3], s16 *dist, s16 *focal, const CamRestrict *r) -- Clamps and overrides the desired values using a CamRestrict record. - Pitch is clamped to [r->pitchMin, r->pitchMax]; when it is clamped and r->pitchSpeed != 0, speeds[0] = pitchSpeed. - Yaw is clamped to [yawMin, yawMax]. With MIRRORBETAINTERVAL (flags & 4) the yaw is clamped only if it lies outside both that arc and the arc shifted by 0x800, and the nearer result is taken. When clamped, speeds[1] = r->yawSpeed, or the current mode's yawSpeed if that is 0. - Roll is clamped likewise, and speeds[2] = rollSpeed if it is nonzero. - dist is clamped to [distMin, distMax]. - *focal = r->focal if it is nonzero. Callers: UpdateFollow, UpdateSamChase, UpdateDirected.

name: Camera_SmoothToDesired
comment: void Camera_SmoothToDesired(Camera *cam, Vec3s *ioAngles, const s32 speeds[3], s16 *ioDist, s16 focal, const Vec3s *aimOffset, int onTrajectory) -- SNAP path, taken if g_camFlags 0x6e4384 bit1 (smooth) is clear, OR bit2 (snap) is set, OR 0x6e43f4 bit8 (cut this frame) is set. It copies aimOffset to g_camAimOffset 0x6e435e and focal to g_camFocal 0x6e435c, sets bit1, clears bit3, and leaves the angles and dist as requested, i.e. a cut. SMOOTH path: - g_camAimOffset approaches aimOffset via 0x5468ee (velocity 0x6e4368, 450/s). - Each angle uses Math_ApproachAngle from the cam angle with velocity 0x6e4350/54/58. Max rate is speeds[i]. Accel/decel is g_camModeParams[mode] +0xC for pitch and roll, and +0x10/+0x14 for yaw. The rates are doubled when onTrajectory and again in mode 1. - In mode 5 while 0x6e43f4 bit6 (hit) is set, the rates are speeds>>7 with accel 2, which nearly freezes the camera. - Pitch is clamped to +-0x400. - Distance approaches via 0x546a31 (velocity 0x6e436c) at rate |delta|+500: accel 5000 when moving in, half rate and accel 2500 when moving out (mode 5 while hit: accel 0, or dist-1 if too far). - g_camFlags bit3 = (2*desired <= current). - The focal steps toward the target at 300/s (50/s in mode 0xC) via 0x546acb. Always clears 0x6e43f4 bit8 and calls Screen_SetProjection(g_camFocal).

name: Camera_ClampToTrajectory
comment: void Camera_ClampToTrajectory(Vec3s *ioPos, const u16 *traj, int axis) -- traj = {u16 count; Vec3s pts[count]}. - When traj differs from g_camTrajectory 0x6e4370 it snaps ioPos to the nearer end point and sets the segment index g_camTrajSegment 0x6e4364. - Otherwise it chooses a neighbour of point idx. axis 0: the previous point, or the next one if nearer by Vec3s_DistSq. axis 1: the neighbour on the same X side. axis 2: the neighbour on the same z side. - It projects: t = dot/|seg|^2 in 4.12 (axis 0), or dx/seg.x, or dz/seg.z. - t <= 0 snaps to point idx. t >= 1 clamps to the neighbour and advances idx by one (at most one segment per frame). Otherwise pos = p + seg*t.

name: Camera_FollowTrajectory
comment: void Camera_FollowTrajectory(const u16 *traj, Vec3s *ioAngles, s16 *ioDist, s32 speeds[3], int snapYaw) -- The aim point is reqTarget 0x6e45a0 + g_camAimOffset. The eye is Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles(angles, *dist, aim). The axis is 0 if !snapYaw; otherwise 1 (X) when yaw % 0x800 == 0 and 2 (z) when it is not. It calls Camera_ClampToTrajectory(eye, traj, axis), then Camera_EyeToAngles(eye, angles, dist, aim), then sets speeds[0] = speeds[1]. Used for CameraRestriction TRAJECTORY rail cameras (UpdateFollow, UpdateSamChase, UpdateDirected).

name: Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles
comment: void __cdecl Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles(Vec3s *out, const Vec3s *angles, s16 dist, const Vec3s *origin) -- Returns the point `dist` units away from `origin` along the direction given by `angles`. Builds a Mat34s from the adjusted angles ((-angles[0]) & 0xFFF, (angles[1] + 0x800) & 0xFFF, angles[2]) with 0x526DC6, transforms the vector (0, 0, dist) through it with 0x5275C1, and adds `origin` component-wise into out. The +0x800 on the second angle and the negated first angle are the camera<->world convention fix-up. Named callers Sam_DrawZoneIndicator, Camera_SolveCollision, Camera_UpdateSamChase, Camera_IsPointOnScreen.

name: Camera_EyeToAngles
comment: void Camera_EyeToAngles(const Vec3s *eye, Vec3s *outAngles, s16 *outDist, const Vec3s *target) -- Inverse of Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles, with d = target - eye. - pitch = round(atan2(d.y, sqrt(dx^2+dz^2)) * 651.8986) & 0xfff, using constant 0x5771c8 = 4096/2pi and round-half-away 0x5771c0 (the fmul is in the asm, the decompiler hides it). - yaw = round(atan2(-dx, dz) * 4096/2pi) & 0xfff, written ONLY if the pitch is more than 20 units away from 0x400 (straight overhead). - dist = sqrt(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2). - Roll is not written.

name: Camera_SolveCollision
comment: The collision enable tested is mask 0x2 (bit 1) of 0x6e45e4, not bit 2: asm 0x5554af 'and edx,0x2', 0x5558a9 'and eax,0x2'. 0x2E has that bit set, so the conclusion stands. Everything else as claimed: sweep 0x552e22(cam+0xD0, &0x6e45e8, &delta, &target, &out); hit -> f4 |= 0x40, angles/distance reverted to cam+0xD8..DC / +0xD6; flag 0x20 (f4<<0x1a) with Manhattan move > 0x32 skips the sweep; local_3c is forced to 1 whenever the collision path runs, so 0x55503c recomputes angles+distance from the final eye and writes +0xD0..D4, +0xD8..DC, +0xD6. End of function clears flags 0x20 and 0x80.

name: Camera_TooFarAndCutLogic
comment: TOO-FAR test, thresholds (counter > 7, or > 15 when cam+0xD6 < 200), the (0x6e43f0 & 0xF)==0 gate (0x6e43f0 counts mod 32), the 9-probe yaw fan (0, +-0x200 ... +-0x800 around 0x800 - wolf+0x16, pitch/roll 0), flag 0x100, the 0x3000-tick (3.0 s) timeout and the disable conditions are all confirmed. Corrections/additions: (a) the ordinary counter increment requires, besides local_54 and 'blocked' (refused XZ >= 16 and permitted XZ <= 4, OR flag 0x10 of 0x6e4384 from TOO-FAR, and not 0x6e4388 bit0), that a camera turn is already in progress (0x6e43c8/cc/d0 not all zero); when they are all zero the hit instead starts a 500 ms side-turn (0x6e43d6 = 4). A second increment path exists (state 4, timer < 250, motion mostly along the wall normal). (b) Every gated frame (one in 16) the block ends with counters = 0 AND f4 &= ~0x40 whether or not a cut happened, so the '>7' must be reached inside one 16-frame window (0.27 s at 60 FPS, 0.53 s at 30 FPS). (c) 0x556c6a returns the FARTHEST clear distance (ray 0x51d2eb clear and Coll_BoxGroundQuery == 0) up to the requested distance, not 'the first yaw with any clear distance' at a short range; since in mode 0xC the requested distance is the current cam+0xD6 (flag 0x80 not set), a cut in mode 0xC re-places the eye up to the full current distance behind Ralph - cuts do NOT shorten the distance in the chase camera, whereas in mode 0 the requested distance is ~610. (d) The 3 s timeout timer 0x6e4418 is refreshed whenever the eye->Ralph ray 0x51d2eb is clear, so a far but unobstructed camera never times out.

name: Camera_FindClearDistance
comment: s16 Camera_FindClearDistance(const Vec3s *target, const Vec3s *angles, s16 maxDist) -- Walks outward from target along angles in steps of (boxMax.x - boxMin.x)/4 = 25 units. For each step it stops at the first step whose segment prev->cur is blocked (Collide_SegmentClearStatic < 0x7fffffff). Otherwise, if the camera box at cur is free (Coll_BoxGroundQuery(box, &y, 0, mode 3, 0) == 0), it records that distance. It returns the farthest free distance below maxDist, or 0. Used by the cut fan in Camera_SolveCollision.

name: Camera_UpdateSamChase
comment: Camera mode 0xC update (only caller Camera_Update 0x55a3d0 case 0xC). Desired distance is seeded with the current distance cam+0xD6 (no restoring distance). Eye = target + R(angles)*dist; then Sam-visibility push; eye height = cam+0xD2 + clamp-ish step toward 0x6e45b6 (delta < -20 -> -10, delta > 10 -> +20, else delta; per frame); eye X clamped to [0x6e45c0,0x6e45c4], Z to [0x6e45c2,0x6e45c6] (with a 30-unit hysteresis offset 0x6e4614/0x6e4618); then 0x55503c converts the eye back to pitch/yaw/distance and 0x5551e8 solves collision.

name: Camera_UpdateFollow
comment: Normal camera (modes 0, 2, 6). Desired distance = mode-table distance (+0x18 of the 0x1C-byte record; 610 for mode 0) plus zoom offset 0x6e43d4, or 0x6e45ae when the Wolf supplies one; only when dist <= 800 and the camera recently collided does it hold/average the current distance. This restoring distance is what mode 0xC lacks.

name: Camera_UpdateRocket
comment: void Camera_UpdateRocket(Camera *cam, Pad *pad) -- Camera mode 3, requested by WOLF_ST_ROCKET_FLY 0x54 and WOLF_ST_ROCKET_CRASH 0x55 (descriptor byte [3] = 3). - Angles = (reqRot.pitch + g_camMinPitch) & 0xfff, reqRot.yaw, reqRot.roll. Wolf_UpdateCamera fills these with half the rocket's pitch and roll. - dist = g_camReqDist 0x6e45ae, or the mode distance 510. - focal = g_camReqFocal 0x6e459e, or 321. - Calls Camera_SmoothToDesired(speeds = mode 3 record, aim offset = request offset), then Camera_SolveCollision(collide = !(g_camFlags & 4), maxVert 32000). - No pad input.

name: Camera_UpdateLook
comment: void Camera_UpdateLook(Camera *cam, Pad *pad) -- Camera mode 1, first-person look on the view button. - Input comes from the right stick, else the left stick, else the d-pad, else the camL/camR masks (0x57eb88/8a). Any input sets g_camFlags bit0 and calls Camera_OnManualRotate(h). - The base rotation is (0, reqYaw) until bit0 is set, then the camera's own rotation. pitch += v*g_dt*1600 and yaw -= h*g_dt*2400 (mode 1 record). - Pitch is clamped to +-0x2aa (60 deg). Distance is the mode distance 0 and focal 384. - Calls Camera_SmoothToDesired, then Camera_SolveCollision(collide = 0). - Then Camera_IsEyeClear(cam, aim point) sets 0x6e43f4 bit7 when the eye is NOT clear (this forces a cut when follow resumes), and g_camLookTime 0x6e441c = g_gameTime.

name: Camera_IsEyeClear
comment: bool Camera_IsEyeClear(const Camera *cam, const Vec3s *target) -- Returns 1 if the segment cam->pos -> target is clear (Collide_SegmentClearStatic == 0x7fffffff) AND the camera box (0x6e45e8/0x6e45f0 around the eye) passes Coll_BoxGroundQuery(mode 3) == 0. Otherwise the low 16 bits are 0.

name: Camera_UpdateFixedLookAt
comment: void Camera_UpdateFixedLookAt(Camera *cam) -- Camera mode 4, requested by WOLF_ST_DIE_BLOWN_AWAY, WOLF_ST_ROCKET_MOUNT and WOLF_ST_ROCKET_IGNITE. The eye does not move. It aims at reqTarget + g_camAimOffset: pitch and yaw come from atan2 as in Camera_EyeToAngles (yaw always written), roll = 0, dist = 3D distance. g_camFocal steps toward the mode focal (321) at 300/s. Then Screen_SetProjection, Camera_ShakeOffset and Camera_BuildViewMatrix(cam, shake).

name: Camera_UpdateScriptedHold
comment: void Camera_UpdateScriptedHold(Camera *cam) -- Camera mode 7, the static scripted pose. It only applies Camera_ShakeOffset and Camera_BuildViewMatrix(cam, shake). The pose itself is written into cam by Camera_StartScripted, or left by the end of a mode 9/10 blend.

name: Camera_UpdateDirected
comment: void Camera_UpdateDirected(Camera *cam, Pad *pad) -- Camera mode 5, for Wolf descriptor camera values 0xD..0x14 (elastic pull, cover, sidle, fishing, pit/zap deaths, caught by Sam) that Wolf_UpdateCamera maps to 5. - Angles come from the request 0x6e45b8/ba/bc. - If request flag 0x10 is set, the player may turn: the kept yaw is used once g_camFlags bit0 is set, and stick/camL/camR input calls Camera_OnManualRotate and sets yaw = cam yaw + input*g_dt*yawSpeed*2. - dist = reqDist or the mode distance (400); focal = reqFocal or 384. - If g_camRestriction is set and request flag 0x20 is set, it calls Camera_ApplyRestriction and then Camera_FollowTrajectory (snapYaw = 0), or resets the trajectory state. - Then Camera_SmoothToDesired and Camera_SolveCollision(collide = !(g_camFlags & 4), 32000).

name: Camera_UpdateOrbit_Unused
comment: void Camera_UpdateOrbit_Unused(Camera *cam, Pad *pad) -- DEAD CODE: the update for camera mode 11. Its parameters are g_camModeParams[11] at 0x6e455c: (300, 1200, 800), dist 400, focal 384. Camera_Update's jump table sends mode 11 to the default case, and nothing references this function. - Yaw input comes from the stick or the camL/camR masks. - With no input it targets cam yaw +-0x400 in the sign of g_camYawVel 0x6e4354, at yawSpeed/4: a continuous slow orbit. - pitch = g_camMinPitch, dist = 400. - Then Camera_SmoothToDesired and Camera_SolveCollision(collide = 0).

name: Camera_EaseLerp
comment: s16 Camera_EaseLerp(s16 from, s16 to, const u8 *curve, u16 t, u16 tBits, u16 curveBits) -- idx = t >> (tBits - curveBits), capped at 2^curveBits - 1. w = curve[idx]*256. Returns (to*w + (0x10000 - w)*from) >> 16. All callers pass curve 0x57e7a0, tBits 10 and curveBits 8. The table peaks at 255, so the weight never exceeds 255/256.

name: Camera_EaseLerpVec3s
comment: void Camera_EaseLerpVec3s(Vec3s *io, const Vec3s *to, const u8 *curve, u16 t, u16 tBits, u16 curveBits) -- In place: io = lerp(io, to, curve[t>>2]/256) per component, with the same indexing as Camera_EaseLerp. Callers: modes 8, 9 and 10, for eye position and aim offset.

name: Camera_EaseLerpAngles
comment: void Camera_EaseLerpAngles(Vec3s *out, const Vec3s *from, const Vec3s *to, const u8 *curve, u16 t, u16 tBits, u16 curveBits) -- out[i] = (from[i] + ((wrap(to[i]-from[i]) * w) >> 16)) & 0xfff, where wrap maps the difference into +-0x800 (shortest turn). The asm uses an unsigned >>16, but the result is equivalent after truncation to s16 and & 0xfff.

name: Camera_EaseFocal
comment: void Camera_EaseFocal(s16 from, s16 to, u16 t) -- g_camFocal 0x6e435c = Camera_EaseLerp(from, to, g_camEaseCurve 0x57e7a0, t, 10, 8), then Screen_SetProjection(this = 0x6d6fe0, g_camFocal).

name: Camera_UpdateScriptReturn
comment: void Camera_UpdateScriptReturn(Camera *cam) -- Camera mode 8, a 1 s eased return from a scripted pose. t = ((g_gameTime - g_camScriptStartTime) & 0x3fffff) >> 2, so 0x400 = 0x1000 ticks = 1 s. - g_camAimOffset is lerped IN PLACE toward the request offset. - The destination rotation is the look-at from the current eye to the aim point (roll 0), or the pre-script rotation 0x6e43be/c2 when g_camScriptFlags & 8. - The destination eye is Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles(destRot, g_camPreScriptDist 0x6e43c4, aim). - eye = EaseLerp(g_camScriptEye 0x6e4398 -> destination); rotation = EaseLerpAngles(g_camScriptRot 0x6e439e -> destRot); focal = EaseFocal(0x6e43a4 -> g_camPreScriptFocal 0x6e43bc). dist = the actual distance. g_camDistVel is zeroed. - Shake, then BuildViewMatrix. - When t >= 0x400: g_camFlags = (flags & ~1) | 2 and g_camMode = g_camScriptReturnMode 0x6e43ac. If t < 0x400 and (flags & 0xa) == 0 it exits at once with bits 0 and 1 cleared.

name: Camera_UpdateScriptBlendIn
comment: void Camera_UpdateScriptBlendIn(Camera *cam) -- Camera mode 9, an eased blend into a scripted pose. t = (g_gameTime - start)*0x400 / g_camScriptBlendTime 0x6e4394, an unsigned divide with no zero check. - g_camAimOffset is lerped in place. - The start eye keeps following: Vec3s_OffsetAlongAngles(preScriptRot 0x6e43be, preScriptDist, current aim). - eye = EaseLerp(start -> g_camScriptEye); rotation = EaseLerpAngles(preScriptRot -> g_camScriptRot); dist = the eye's distance to the aim point. - The focal eases from 0x6e43a4 to 0x6e43a4 (both arguments are the same global in the asm at 0x559b0b/0x559b13), so the FOV does not blend. - When t >= 0x400: Camera_SetMode(7, 1).

name: Camera_UpdateScriptToScript
comment: void Camera_UpdateScriptToScript(Camera *cam) -- Camera mode 10, an eased blend from the snapshot taken when a new script (flag 4) replaced an active one to the new scripted pose. t = (g_gameTime - start)*0x400 / g_camScriptBlendTime. eye = EaseLerp(0x6e43a6 -> g_camScriptEye); rotation = EaseLerpAngles(0x6e43ae -> g_camScriptRot); focal = EaseFocal(0x6e43b4 -> 0x6e43a4). Then shake and BuildViewMatrix. When t >= 0x400: Camera_SetMode(7, 1).

name: Camera_ResetMotion
comment: void Camera_ResetMotion(void) -- Zeroes the velocities 0x6e4350/54/58 (angles), 0x6e4368 (aim offset) and 0x6e436c (distance), the auto-turn rates 0x6e43c8/cc/d0, zoom-out 0x6e43d4, turn state 0x6e43d6, the probe and pitch-adjust states and timers (0x6e43df/d7 low 3 bits, 0x6e43e2, 0x6e43e4, 0x6e43ee), the frame counter 0x6e43f0, the blocked counters 0x6e43f1/0x6e4420, the hit frames 0x6e43de and the Sam push timer 0x6e43fa. It sets 0x6e43ec = 100 and 0x6e43fc = 3000, sets 0x6e4418 and 0x6e441c to g_gameTime, and clears 0x6e4388 bit0. In 0x6e43f4 it clears bits 0-4, 6 and 8 and SETS bit5 (0x20: the next solver call may jump more than 50 units without a sweep). It invalidates the block positions 0x6e440c/0x6e4412 and 0x6e4400..04 (0x8000). Callers: Camera_SetMode (modes 0/6, 4, 7) and Camera_Reset.

name: Camera_SetMode
comment: (u8 mode, u8 flag). Case 0xC only sets g_camMode = 0xC, clears low 10 bits of 0x6e43f8 (Sam visibility counter), bits 0..2 of 0x6e43f4 and timer 0x6e43fa; it does NOT call the reset 0x559c49. Cases 0/6 (unless leaving scripted modes 7/9), 4 and 7 call 0x559c49, which zeroes blocked counters and sets 0x6e43f4 |= 0x20 (allow one non-colliding jump). So leaving a chase resets/unsticks the camera; entering one never does.

name: Camera_Reset
comment: void Camera_Reset(void) -- Full camera reset, from Wolf_Reset 0x487ea2 and Camera_InitSettings. - g_camera: eye (0, -400, 0), dist 0x400, rotation 0. - Request block cleared: target, velocity, aim offset, rotation, dist/focal overrides. Speed factor 0x6e45a6 = 0x1000. Only caller ScnBody_RenderEx (used by Sam_DrawZoneIndicator and 0x439b8e/0x45e323/0x4abec3/0x506560, with projDist 0x180 or 400).

name: PackJpeg_Prev
comment: bool __thiscall PackJpeg_Prev(PackJpeg *this) -- Unsigned guard on index != 0, decrement, PackJpeg_SetIndex, then sete on index==0 ('now at the first picture'). Sole caller is the bonus gallery's Left-arrow arm, which loads ecx = g_packJpeg 0x7195d8 and ignores the return, so the boolean is dead in this build.

name: PackJpeg_Next
comment: bool __thiscall PackJpeg_Next(PackJpeg *this) -- Unsigned compare of index against count-1, increment, SetIndex, sete on index==count-1. Sole caller the Right-arrow arm, guarded by the same unsigned test on the same two globals. Latent: with count==0, count-1 is 0xFFFFFFFF and both the guard and this test pass, so the index would run past the table - no shipped pack has count 0 (counts range from 8 to 25).

name: PackJpeg_Close
comment: void __thiscall PackJpeg_Close(PackJpeg *this) -- Clears the open flag, frees and nulls the entry table, then fclose on fp - which it does NOT null, leaving a dangling FILE*. Exact mirror of PackJpeg_Open. Sole caller the gallery's exit arm, right after PackJpeg_ReleaseImage.

name: PackJpeg_SelectByName
comment: bool __thiscall PackJpeg_SelectByName(PackJpeg *this, const char *name) -- Linear scan calling Str_IsPrefixOf on entries + i*0x18 + 9, which is exactly where the shipped .sdw files hold the name. The argument direction follows from the push order: the query is pushed first and the entry name last, so under cdecl arg0 is the STORED name and the test is 'the entry name is a prefix of the query'. In Intro.sdw the 15-char names are unterminated and sit on the prefix side, so a compare runs into the next record.

name: PackJpeg_SelectAndFetch
comment: bool __thiscall PackJpeg_SelectAndFetch(PackJpeg *this, const char *name, void *out) -- SelectByName, then memcpy 4 bytes from this+0x10 to the out pointer, ret 8. What it fetches cannot be established: this+0x10 is written by no instruction anywhere in the image, so the 4 bytes are uninitialised. Dead: zero calls and zero occurrences of the dword 0x0055dc0d, so no table entry either.

name: PackJpeg_Open
comment: bool __thiscall PackJpeg_Open(PackJpeg *this, const char *pathNoExt) -- Str_Concat2 with the '.SDW' literal, fopen 'rb', fread the 12-byte header straight over this+0/+4/+8, malloc(count*0x18) and fread the entry table, SetIndex(0), open flag = 1. All six shipped Bonus/*.sdw parse with this layout (version 0x301, word2 0, counts 8-25, 0x18-byte records, every fileOffset landing on the JFIF magic). The caller's path prefix is not a string literal: it pushes 0x6cf460, a runtime buffer filled at load with g_pathBonus '.\Bonus\'.

name: PackJpeg_SetIndex
comment: int __thiscall PackJpeg_SetIndex(PackJpeg *this, u32 index) -- The whole body is `mov [this+0x1c], arg; xor eax,eax; ret 4`. Four callers, all in this block. The field it writes is the same 0x7195f4 the bonus menu and footer read directly.

name: PackJpeg_DecodeToTextures
comment: void __thiscall PackJpeg_DecodeToTextures(PackJpeg *this, int unused) -- operator new for the decode buffer, fseek, Jpeg_DecodeToRgb555Flipped, then lock four 256x256 textures and split the 512x480 image into quadrants with a hardcoded 0x200 pitch. ret 4 but the body contains zero [ebp+…] references, so the pushed 0 is unused. The decode buffer leaks: the only calls are operator new, fseek, the decoder, 4 locks, the memcpys and 4 unlocks, with no free, so 491,520 bytes leak per picture shown, and both arrow arms re-set the redecode flag, so it leaks on every Left/Right press. Two further defects: the first memcpy loop runs 241 times so the seam row is duplicated and the last image row never displays, and lPitch is never read, so the 0x200 stride is an unguarded driver assumption.

name: PackJpeg_BeginImage
comment: void __thiscall PackJpeg_BeginImage(PackJpeg *this) -- malloc(0x28) for the image record, fseek, Jpeg_GetDimensions, writes w/h as s16 and byteSize = w*h*2, then creates any missing 256x256 Texture. On failure it shows a MessageBox but RETURNS VOID without stopping the state machine, so the caller still advances to the decode, which then runs with an uninitialised byteSize and four null texture pointers. Note the width/height/byteSize fields are read with movsx and cdq throughout, so they are signed, not the unsigned types proposed.

name: PackJpeg_ReleaseImage
comment: void __thiscall PackJpeg_ReleaseImage(PackJpeg *this) -- free(this->img) without nulling it, then the scalar deleting destructor on each of the four texture slots, zeroing each. The double-free hazard is real but unreachable: every ReleaseImage in the bonus menu is followed by Close or BeginImage. Together with BeginImage this makes the gallery destroy and recreate all four DirectDraw textures on every picture change.

name: PackJpeg_DrawImage
comment: void __thiscall PackJpeg_DrawImage(PackJpeg *this) -- Letterboxes from the image aspect against the frustum viewport, then four Draw2D_TexRect_Immediate quads in TL/TR/BL/BR order matching the tile assignment derived from the memcpy loops and the bottom-up decode. All float constants read from the image. Latent bug confirmed: the horizontal seam is computed as (x1-x0)/2, half the WIDTH rather than the centre - correct only because the fit-to-width branch zeroes x0 for every landscape image, which every shipped 512x480 picture is.

name: Pad_DetectType
comment: void Pad_DetectType(Pad *pad) -- If InputMgr_IsDeviceDigital(&g_obj6d6780, 0) == 1, sets pad+0x57 = pad+0x58 = 4 (PS1 digital-pad id). Otherwise clears bytes +0x59, +0x5a, +0x5b, +0x54 and dwords +0x44, +0x48, +0x4c, +0x60, then sets +0x57 = +0x58 = 7 (analog/DualShock id). Only caller Pad_ReadRaw, so it runs every Input_Poll.

name: Pad_ReadRaw
comment: void Pad_ReadRaw(Pad *pad) -- Fills the 8-byte PS1-style receive frame at pad+0. Sets right-stick bytes +4/+5 = 0x80, then calls InputMgr_Poll(&g_obj6d6780). On failure (<0): status +0 = 1 and nothing else changes, so the buttons are stale. On success: calls Pad_DetectType(&g_pad) (hard-coded g_pad, not the argument); status = 0; high nibble of +1 = (g_pad+0x57 & 0xf), low nibble kept; +6/+7 = InputMgr axisX/axisY (0x6d6784/85); +2 = InputMgr padBits (0x6d6786). Only caller Input_Poll(&g_pad); g_pad2 is never read.

name: Pad_InitPair
comment: void Pad_InitPair(Pad *p1, Pad *p2) -- Sets p1+0x5b = p2+0x5b = 0 and g_padRepeatDelay 0x719622 = 500 ms, then Pad_ResetState on both. Called by Input_Init with g_pad and g_pad2.

name: PadFrame_Clear
comment: void PadFrame_Clear(u8 *frame) -- Resets one 8-byte pad frame to idle: u16 +2 = 0xffff (all buttons released, active-low) and u16 +4 = +6 = 0x8080 (both sticks centred). The status and type bytes are left alone.

name: Pad_ClearFrames
comment: void Pad_ClearFrames(Pad *pad) -- Calls PadFrame_Clear on pad+0x2a (current frame), pad+0x22 (previous frame) and pad+0 (raw frame). Called by Input_Init for g_pad and g_pad2.

name: Input_Reacquire
comment: void Input_Reacquire(void) -- InputMgr_SetAcquiredAll(&g_obj6d6780, 1), then Input_SetMode(0). No direct caller and no pointer reference anywhere in the exe.

name: Input_Unacquire
comment: void Input_Unacquire(void) -- InputMgr_SetAcquiredAll(&g_obj6d6780, 0): releases every DirectInput device. Sole caller Load_FreeLevel 0x54818f.

name: Input_GetMode
comment: u8 Input_GetMode(void) -- Returns g_inputMode 0x719620 (0 live, 1 record, 2 playback). No callers.

name: Input_EmptyStub
comment: void Input_EmptyStub(void) -- 5-byte empty function (push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; ret). No callers or pointer references.

name: Input_ApplyControlConfig
comment: void Input_ApplyControlConfig(ControlConfig *cfg) -- Switches on the u8 preset at cfg+0 (jump table 0x55eda0) and calls Input_ApplyRemap(slot0xc, slot0xd, slot0xe, slot0xf, slot0xb, slot0xa). Preset 0 = (0xefff Triangle, 0xdfff Circle, 0xbfff Cross, 0x7fff Square, 0xf7ff R1, 0xfbff L1). Preset 1 = (Square, Triangle, Circle, Cross, R1, L1). Preset 2 = (Cross, Square, Triangle, Circle, R1, L1). Preset 3 = custom words cfg+8, +0xa, +4, +6, +0xc, +0xe. Other values do nothing. Sole caller 0x50bddc (the Progress options apply), which passes Progress+0x9a. The slots are view/run/action/jump/sneak/inventory, so the three presets only rotate the four face buttons.

name: Input_StoreControlConfig
comment: void Input_StoreControlConfig(ControlConfig *cfg) -- Inverse of preset 3. Writes the live map into cfg via Input_GetMapping: +8 = slot 0xc, +0xa = 0xd, +4 = 0xe, +6 = 0xf, +0xc = 0xb, +0xe = 0xa. No callers or pointer references.

name: Pad_ResetState
comment: void __fastcall Pad_ResetState(Pad *this) -- Zeroes bytes +0x57, +0x58, +0x59, +0x5a, +0x5c, +0x5d, +0x54 and dwords +0x44, +0x48, +0x4c, +0x60; sets u16 +0x50 = 0x1000. Only caller Pad_InitPair.

name: Pad_Latch_Dup
comment: void __fastcall Pad_Latch_Dup(Pad *this) -- Instruction-for-instruction duplicate of Pad_Latch 0x55ef9f. Forces raw buttons |= 6 (L3/R3 released), or 0xffff when Pad_IsConnected fails; Pad_AutoRepeat(this+0x36, cur.buttons); Pad_AnalogToDpadBits; copies cur(+0x2a..+0x31) to prev(+0x22..) and raw(+0..+7) to cur. No callers or references.

name: Pad_GetChangedPress
comment: u16 __thiscall Pad_GetChangedPress(Pad *this, u16 ignoreMask) -- Returns cur.buttons (+0x2c) when all three hold: cur.status (+0x2a) == 0, cur.buttons != prev.buttons (+0x24), and (cur.buttons | ignoreMask) != 0xffff (some non-ignored button is down). Otherwise returns 0xffff. Sole caller 0x4ef717, which uses g_pad and mask 0xff0f so only d-pad changes count.

name: Pad_Stub_55f078
comment: void __thiscall Pad_Stub_55f078(Pad *this, u32 arg) -- Empty __thiscall body with one stack argument (ret 4); neighbour of Pad_Rumble_stub. No callers. Probably a stubbed PS1 libpad call (inferred).

name: Pad_OnConnected_stub
comment: void __thiscall Pad_OnConnected_stub(Pad *this) -- Empty __thiscall body (ret). Input_Poll calls it on g_pad whenever Pad_JustConnected is true, so the 'pad plugged in' hook is a no-op on PC.

name: Pad_Stub_55f09d
comment: void __thiscall Pad_Stub_55f09d(Pad *this) -- Empty __thiscall body (ret). No callers or references.

name: Pad_Open
comment: void __thiscall Pad_Open(Pad *this, int port) -- Retries InputMgr_Poll up to 60 (0x3c) times until it returns >= 0; returns if all 60 fail. Otherwise runs the same type detection as Pad_DetectType, but on this (digital: +0x57 = +0x58 = 4; else clear state and 7). The port argument is unused. Input_Init passes 0 for g_pad and 0x10 for g_pad2, which are the PlayStation libpad port numbers.

name: Pad_TypeChanged
comment: int __thiscall Pad_TypeChanged(Pad *this) -- Returns 1 if the current type nibble (+0x2b >> 4) and the previous one (+0x23 >> 4) are both non-zero and differ. When it is true, Input_Poll writes Progress+0x9c = (type == 7).

name: Pad_JustConnected
comment: int __thiscall Pad_JustConnected(Pad *this) -- Returns 1 if the current type nibble (+0x2b >> 4) is non-zero and the previous one (+0x23 >> 4) is zero. When it is true, Input_Poll calls Pad_OnConnected_stub.

name: Reg_DeleteSubKey
comment: u8 Reg_DeleteSubKey(LPCSTR name) -- Reg_OpenAppRoot(&k); RegDeleteKeyA(k, name); returns 1 only if both succeed. Always Reg_CloseKey2(&k). No callers.

name: Reg_SubKeyExists
comment: u8 Reg_SubKeyExists(LPCSTR name) -- RegOpenKeyExA chain HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (0x80000002) \ SOFTWARE \ Infogrames \ Sheep Dog'n Wolf DX7 \ name, each with KEY_ALL_ACCESS 0x2001f. Returns 1 if the final open succeeds. It reuses one HKEY variable for every level and closes only the last one, so the three parent keys leak. No callers.

name: Scenaric_ResetAll
comment: Calls vtable+0x14 (Reset) on every entry of g_scnObjects, then on the extra dynamic entries of g_scnActive beyond index g_scnObjectCount. Called from Fade_Update 0x53e8a3 when the fade timer 0x6ddf70 (1/4096 s units, decremented by g_dt) reaches 0 and g_gameFlags&0x800 is clear. This is the restart/retry path.

name: Scenaric_UpdateAll
comment: As claimed. One addition for cinematic mode (0x71c458 != 0 && 0x71c450 != 0): the condition is (eligible && !(flags&0x80)) || ((flags&0x80) && (flags&0x20)). An object with both 0x80 and 0x20 set is therefore updated even when it fails the distance test or has 0x2000 (never-update) set, so the cinematic override bypasses the activity radius. obj+0x34 (u32 dist^2) is written for every active object regardless. The compare is unsigned.

name: Scenaric_RenderAll
comment: Iterates g_scnActive and calls vtable+8 (Render) with &g_camera (0x584c50). An object is rendered when obj+0x34 (dist^2, set by UpdateAll) < (farDist + radius(obj+0x2e))^2, it passes a view-plane test (or has flag 0x10), (flags&0x804)==0 and byte obj+0x12==0. So flags 0x800 and 0x004 mean hidden.

name: Game_Frame_2
comment: As claimed, with fixes: when menu state is 2..5 it calls FUN_0053fe7f (a thunk to FUN_005402ff) and SKIPS Game_SelectMenuAnim, Game_UpdateAndDraw (so no world update AND no world render, no Fade_Update) and the pause-menu update. The Select-button open path also requires FUN_005644b0()==0 (stream state not 3..6) and FUN_00536369()!=0 (object flag 0x10 set and byte +0x1c == 0). Hotkeys 0x6d678b/0x6d678a additionally require menu state 0 or 7 and FUN_005400f2()==0. FUN_0055f55f(mask) tests (0x71965a & ~mask)==0 && (0x71965c & ~mask)!=0 - 'newly pressed' is an interpretation of those two pad words that was not verified. Note FUN_0055f55f(0xefff) is also OR-ed with key byte 0x6d678b==1, i.e. the pause hotkey doubles as the pad-0xefff (menu confirm) key.

name: WarReloc_GetIdAt
comment: u16 WarReloc_GetIdAt(u16 index) -- Clamps index to g_warRelocCount-1 and returns the low word (the cinematic id) of g_warRelocTable[index].word0. Returns 0xffff when the table is empty (count-1 truncates to 0xffff). No callers.

name: Scn_FindIdList
comment: (u16 id, u16 *countOut): linear search of the table at *0x71af54 (entry count at 0x71af58). Each entry is a header dword (low 16 bits = id, high 16 bits = element count n) followed by n dwords of pointers. Returns a pointer to the first element, or NULL with count 0. 70 callers. This is how box-list and trajectory properties become object pointer arrays.

name: IdList_GetBlob
comment: u32 *IdList_GetBlob(u32 *countOut) -- If g_idListBlob 0x71af5c != NULL: *countOut = g_idListCount and returns the blob. Otherwise returns NULL and leaves *countOut untouched. Sole caller Res_FindBitmapGroup 0x53b47b.

name: IdList_Next
comment: u32 *IdList_Next(u32 *rec) -- Steps to the next packed id-list record: rec + (rec[0] >> 16) + 1 dwords (the header plus count entries). NULL maps to NULL. Sole caller Res_FindBitmapGroup.

name: IdList_GetId
comment: u16 IdList_GetId(const u16 *rec) -- Returns rec[0] (the record id), or 0 for NULL. Sole caller Res_FindBitmapGroup.

name: TexScroll_AddRect
comment: void TexScroll_AddRect(const u16 *rec, s8 step) -- Fills entry e = g_texScrolls 0x71af80 + g_texScrollCount*0x18 from rec {x, w, y, h, texPage}: e+4 = x, +6 = y, +8 = w, +0xa = h, +0xc = +0xe = 0, +0x10 = w, +0x12 = h, +0x14 offset = 0, +0x15 = step, +0x16 = texPage. tex = g_pPolyBatcher->+0x14[texPage]. Allocates a 0x90-byte surface object (operator new, ctor 0x40a140(g_pD3DApp, w, h, tex->+0xc)) into g_texScrollBackup[count] 0x71b288. Then IDirectDrawSurface7::BltFast (vtable +0x1c) copies RECT {x, y, x+w, y+h} of the texture into the backup at (0,0). g_texScrollCount++. There is no capacity check.

name: TexScroll_Update
comment: void TexScroll_Update(u16 index) -- Scrolls one rect by one row. offset = (offset + step + backup->height (surface+8)) % backup->height, stored in an s8. Locks the texture (Surface_LockForWrite, flags 0x821) and the backup (0x40ae0a, flags 0x811) into two freshly new'd 0x7c-byte DDSURFACEDESC2 buffers. memcpy's backup rows 0..h-offset to texture rows y+offset.., then (if offset != 0) rows h-offset..h to rows y..: a vertical wrap-around shift. Texels are 16-bit, and the row stride is the surface WIDTH (surface+4) rather than the lock's lPitch. Unlocks both and deletes both desc buffers.

name: TexScroll_Init
comment: void TexScroll_Init(void) -- g_texScrollCount = 0. If the four u16 list ids at 0x6ddf60..0x6ddf66 (from the WAR type-0x83 header) sum to non-zero, calls TexScroll_AddList(id[i], (g_texScrollReverseMask 0x6ddf68 >> i) & 1) for i = 0..3. Called from Load_DAVnWAR at 0x547f37 with no ECX set up, so Ghidra's __fastcall is wrong: it is void(void).

name: TexScroll_FreeAll
comment: void TexScroll_FreeAll(void) -- For i < g_texScrollCount: if g_texScrollBackup[i] is non-NULL, calls its vtable slot 0 (scalar deleting dtor) with 1. Then g_texScrollCount = 0. The pointers are not NULLed. Sole caller Load_FreeLevel 0x54818f.

name: Time_Init
comment: Allocates the 0x28-byte Timer (Timer_Construct) into g_pTimer, latches it, sets g_timeScale = 0x1000 (1.0 in 4.12 fixed point) and zeroes every clock: g_dt, g_dtRaw, g_gameTime, g_rawTime, the ms variants and g_framesThisSecond. Its only caller is the level loader 0x547855, right before Scenaric_RegisterAllClasses, so all clocks restart on every level load. This is the ONLY write to g_timeScale in the exe and Time_Update is the only reader, so the time scale is constant 1.0; there is no built-in slow-motion or fast-forward. It also sets DAT_0071b2f8 = 1, which 0x49bd01 and 0x4d4445 toggle between 0 and 1 but which has no direct reader.

name: Time_RestartTimer
comment: void Time_RestartTimer(void) -- Timer_Start(g_pTimer). No callers.

name: Time_Pause
comment: void Time_Pause(void) -- g_timePausedDelta (double at 0x71b2f0) = -Timer_GetDelta(g_pTimer, TIMER_TICKS), then Timer_Stop(g_pTimer). Ghidra shows an empty body because the delta is returned in ST0 (fchs; fstp qword). Sole caller is the stream-player update 0x563bd0, right before it busy-waits for the loader thread.

name: Time_Resume
comment: void Time_Resume(void) -- Timer_Start(g_pTimer), then Timer_OffsetBase(g_pTimer, g_timePausedDelta), which moves the base back by the unconsumed pre-pause delta. The next Time_Update sees only that delta, and the stall is dropped from every clock. Sole caller 0x563bd0, after the wait.

name: Str_CopyNoTerm
comment: u16 Str_CopyNoTerm(char *dst, const char *src) -- Copies bytes until src's NUL WITHOUT writing a terminator and returns the count (u16). No callers.

name: Str_CopyAsciiN
comment: u16 Str_CopyAsciiN(char *dst, const char *src, u16 max) -- Copies up to max bytes, stopping early at the first byte with the high bit set (signed < 0). It does NOT stop at NUL and writes no terminator. Returns the count. Sole caller Save_InitCardHeader 0x54a6fb, which copies the 2-byte 'SC' card magic.

name: Str_CopyPadZero
comment: void Str_CopyPadZero(char *dst, const char *src, u8 size) -- Copies src up to (not including) its NUL with no bound, then zero-fills dst from there up to size. A src longer than size overruns. No callers.

name: Vec3i_SetLength
comment: void Vec3i_SetLength(s32 v[3], s32 len) -- sq = x*x + y*y + z*z in s32; returns unchanged if sq == 0. Otherwise mag = __ftol(sqrt((double)sq)) (0x566594, 0x565d1c) and v[i] = v[i]*len/mag with idiv. Sole caller 0x47255f, which passes a byte field (movzx) as len.

name: VideoPlayer_StaticInit
comment: void VideoPlayer_StaticInit(void) -- _initterm entry (pointer at 0x5790c4): calls VideoPlayer_StaticInit_Construct, then VideoPlayer_StaticInit_RegisterDtor.

name: VideoPlayer_StaticInit_Construct
comment: void VideoPlayer_StaticInit_Construct(void) -- Calls ctor 0x421ba0 on g_videoPlayer 0x71c328 (ECX = 0x71c328). The ctor sets vtable 0x5744e0, +4 = 0, +8 = 0, +0x10c = 0 and clears 0x6cc85c. Video_PlaySequence then uses this object through 0x421c30(g_pD3DAppMain) and 0x421ce0(path, 1)

name: VideoPlayer_StaticInit_RegisterDtor
comment: void VideoPlayer_StaticInit_RegisterDtor(void) -- atexit(VideoPlayer_StaticDtor 0x561600) via the CRT helper 0x565e26.

name: VideoPlayer_StaticDtor
comment: void VideoPlayer_StaticDtor(void) -- Calls dtor 0x421c00 on g_videoPlayer. The dtor restores vtable 0x5744e0, deletes the object at +0x10c through its vtable slot 0 (arg 1) and clears +8.

name: Cine_Construct
comment: Cine *__fastcall Cine_Construct(Cine *this) -- NOT A GHIDRA FUNCTION (needs seeding). Zeroes +0 (tracks), u16 +8, +0xc, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c, +0x8a8 (cineId), +0x8b0, +0x8ac and +0x958 (attachCount). Sets flags +0x8b4 = 0x0c000000 (default: auto-find CINSHEEPBBOX and CINBBOX). Returns this in EAX. Reached only through the _initterm thunk 0x5634b0.

name: Cine_FindFirstPosKeyFor
comment: Vec3s *__thiscall Cine_FindFirstPosKeyFor(Cine *this, ScnObject *obj) -- Cine_SaveIterator, Cine_ResetIterators, then walks records (Cine_AdvanceScriptCursor) until one has opcode 1 on a track whose target (track+4) == obj. Returns record+10: the Vec3s of the record's first inline key, past the 8-byte header and the key's u16 time. If the script runs out, it restores the iterator and returns NULL. On success the iterator is NOT restored. Sole caller Cine_Start with g_pWolf, for the flag-0x10 world offset.

name: Cine_FindFirstPosKey
comment: Vec3s *__fastcall Cine_FindFirstPosKey(Cine *this) -- Same search as Cine_FindFirstPosKeyFor (opcode 1), for the current track's target (targetDesc+4), captured before the rewind. Restores the iterator only on failure. Sole caller Cine_NotifyActors, when the target is g_pWolf.

name: Cine_FindFirstRotKey
comment: Vec3s *__fastcall Cine_FindFirstRotKey(Cine *this) -- As Cine_FindFirstPosKey but for opcode 2 (rotation): returns record+10 of the first rotation record on the current target's track, or NULL with the iterator restored. Sole caller Cine_NotifyActors.

name: Cine_FindCinBBox
comment: void *__fastcall Cine_FindCinBBox(Cine *this) -- Scn_FindIdList(8 = WAR_IDO_CINBBOX from GameRes.h, &n). n == 0: this->cineBox (+0x8b0) = 0 and returns 0; else returns the first entry. Cine_Start calls it when its box argument is 0 and flags & 0x8000000.

name: Cine_FindCinSheepBBox
comment: void *__fastcall Cine_FindCinSheepBBox(Cine *this) -- Scn_FindIdList(9 = WAR_IDO_CINSHEEPBBOX, &n). n == 0: this->sheepBox (+0x8ac) = 0 and returns 0; else returns the first entry. Cine_Start calls it when its sheep-box argument is 0 and flags & 0x4000000.

name: Cine_Load
comment: void __fastcall Cine_Load(Cine *this) -- Clears runFlags bit 0 (+0x24, voice started) and sets claim flag +0x8e4 = 0. res = WarReloc_Find((u16)cineId +0x8a8, &n, &+0x8e4): a read-only lookup that writes back the entry's bit-31 claimed flag. Then +4 = res, +0 = res+4 (first track), u16 +8 = n (track count), u8 +0x974 = 0, +0x8e0 = 0. Calls Cine_ResolveTracks, Cine_TagObjectsInBox and Cine_NotifyActors, then sets +0x8c8 = 1 if any track has selector 0 (camera). res is not NULL-checked. Sole caller Cine_Start.

name: Cine_ResolveTracks
comment: void __fastcall Cine_ResolveTracks(Cine *this) -- Walks tracks with Cine_SkipRecords. Selector 1/2: obj = Scenaric_FindByRecord(g_pDav->+0x10 + (g_pDav->+0xc[track.index] & 0xffffff)), stored in slot this+0x50+k*0x2c (slot.obj) and in track+4; sets obj->flags (+0x3a) |= 0x80; if Cine.flags & 0x40, Cine_SaveActorState(obj, &slot.save); k++. Selector 3/4: track+4 = (*(void***)0x585060)[track.index] (world static object). There is no bound on k.

name: Cine_NotifyActors
comment: If the Wolf is an actor and flags & 0x18 != 0, player+0x20 (0x71c458) is set to 1 immediately and the Wolf gets no message 0x12. The cinematic runs from the next frame with no 0x407 handshake delay. 0x18aa has bit 0x08, so there is no dead time between the fire press and the cinematic being active.

name: Cine_TagObjectsInBox

Add, Remove and Init are as claimed. 0x6cfc72 is an 'all carried items already committed' flag: Init sets it to 1, Add sets it to 0 when a non-kept item is added, and 0x50d37f sets it back to 1. Inventory_Init also caches up to 6 Mailbox objects (class 4) at 0x6cfc54 (count 0x6cfc50). Commit (0x50d37f, called from Wolf HandleMessage 0x484550 case 0x402, which also stores the respawn pos/heading at Wolf+0x6dc..0x6e2) sets flag 8 on every carried item and on the sub-objects of composites, then sends msg 0x600 (arg 1) to the mailboxes. Wolf Reset 0x487ea2 -> 0x50d180: if the flag is 0, it first splits non-kept composite items (Add both parts, msgs 7, 7, 0x2b, 8, Remove the composite), then for every non-kept item does Remove + AddToWorld(NULL) + msg 0x55. It always sends msg 0x55 (arg 1) to the mailboxes.
